_about: Published data for the House as Power Station Provider Explorer. Generated by atlas-tools/build-power-station-provider-universe.py from the Atlas read-back, the official supplier pages re-read on 13 October 2026, and the public wording. Not a ranking, not a recommendation and not a complete list of suppliers. No rates or earnings are carried. Do not hand-edit.

tabs.label: Electricity suppliers
tabs.note: Under Ireland's Clean Export Guarantee, electricity suppliers are required to offer payment for eligible exported electricity, subject to the applicable rules. These are four that PlotNua has checked, not a complete list. The four suppliers listed here require customers to purchase their electricity from them to receive export payments under their published arrangements.

orgs.name: Bord Gáis Energy
orgs.subtitle: Microgen Export Plan
orgs.offers: Pays its own electricity customers for exported electricity under its Microgen Export Plan, as a credit to the electricity bill.
orgs.how: A home that is eligible for a smart meter must have one installed, and ESB Networks must have received an NC6 or equivalent form. A home that is not eligible for a smart meter is paid on a deemed amount, calculated by formula. Payments start after at least three months of export. Its page gives the frequency as four times a year in one place and every six months in another, so confirm it with Bord Gáis Energy. It says its rate is subject to change.
orgs.evidence: Bord Gáis Energy's microgeneration page, checked 13 October 2026

orgs.name: Electric Ireland
orgs.subtitle: Microgeneration Scheme
orgs.offers: Pays its own customers for the electricity their home exports, as a credit on each bill in line with the billing cycle.
orgs.how: To be paid, the home needs a smart meter, and ESB Networks must have been told about the export connection on an NC6 form. Where a home is not eligible for a smart meter, Electric Ireland says it pays on a deemed export calculation instead. It describes its rate as variable and subject to change.
orgs.evidence: Electric Ireland's microgeneration page, checked 13 October 2026

orgs.name: Energia
orgs.subtitle: Microgeneration Scheme
orgs.offers: Credits exported electricity to the bill of a household whose import and export are both with Energia, on the two-monthly bill, as a credit rather than a bank transfer.
orgs.how: A smart meter is needed to join, and Energia says it can request one. The NC6 form must be submitted to ESB Networks, which an installer may do. Readings are taken every thirty minutes, and Energia notes that the export period on a bill can differ from the import period.

orgs.name: Flogas
orgs.subtitle: Micro-generation
orgs.offers: Credits excess exported electricity to a household's Flogas electricity account every two months, with a statement showing whether the credit was metered or deemed.
orgs.how: The household must be registered with Flogas for its import electricity, and ESB Networks must have been informed on an NC6 or equivalent form. A home that is eligible for a smart meter but does not have one is not eligible. A home not currently eligible for one is paid on a deemed amount calculated by ESB Networks. Flogas reserves the right to vary its rate and says it gives thirty days' notice of a change by email or letter.
